extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, patent office staff, and legal practitioners working with South African patents
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory standards and procedural requirements from the Patents Act, 1978 (as amended) governing what is patentable, how patent applications must be made and processed, rights and remedies, agents/attorneys, and administrative procedures in South Africa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (section 25(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may, subject to the provisions of this section, be granted for any new invention which involves an inventive step and which is capable of being used or applied in trade or industry or agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three cumulative requirements: novelty (new), inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability (capable of being used or applied in trade/industry/agriculture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject-matter (section 25(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything which consists of: (a) a discovery; (b) a scientific theory; (c) a mathematical method; (d) a literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work or any other aesthetic creation; (e) a scheme, rule or method for performing a mental act, playing a game or doing business; (f) a program for a computer; or (g) the presentation of information, shall not be an invention for the purposes of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are not inventions 'as such' — the statutory exclusions limit patentability of abstract, aesthetic, mental, business, software-as-such, and information-presentation subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of exclusions (section 25(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of subsection (2) shall prevent, only to the extent to which a patent or an application for a patent relates to that thing as such, anything from being treated as an invention for the purposes of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions apply only to the subject-matter 'as such' — practical technical contributions involving excluded items may still be patentable if not just the excluded thing 'as such'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy and biological exclusions (section 25(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not be granted (a) for an invention the publication or exploitation of which would be generally expected to encourage offensive or immoral behaviour; or (b) for any variety of animal or plant or any essentially biological process for the production of animals or plants, not being a micro-biological process or the product of such a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents refused on grounds of public morality/immorality and for essentially biological processes/plant/animal varieties (micro-biological exceptions noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty defined; state of the art (section 25(5)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be deemed to be new if it does not form part of the state of the art immediately before the priority date of that invention. The state of the art shall comprise all matter which has been made available to the public (in the Republic or elsewhere) by written or oral description, by use or in any other way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is assessed against all public disclosures worldwide before the priority date (including oral disclosures and use).

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art includes public patent applications (section 25(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of the art shall also comprise matter contained in an application, open to public inspection, for a patent, notwithstanding that that application was lodged at the patent office and became open to public inspection on or after the priority date of the relevant invention, if that matter was contained in that application both as lodged and as open to public inspection and the priority date of that matter is earlier than that of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier patent applications open to public inspection can be prior art if they disclose the matter both as lodged and when open and have an earlier priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret commercial use counts as prior art (section 25(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention used secretly and on a commercial scale within the Republic shall also be deemed to form part of the state of the art for the purposes of subsection (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secret but commercial exploitation in South Africa can defeat novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for substances for medical treatment (section 25(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an invention consisting of a substance or composition for use in a method of treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy or of diagnosis practiced on the human or animal body, the fact that the substance or composition forms part of the state of the art immediately before the priority date of the invention shall not prevent a patent being ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute contains a special rule regarding patentability of substances used in medical treatment/diagnosis; text in file truncated. (Guidance: consult full text for precise formulation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply for a patent (heading: section 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory provision exists specifying who may apply for a patent (listed as a distinct section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act contains rules on entitlement to apply (see section 27 in full Act) — e.g., inventors, legal representatives, employers in certain circumstances; extract only provides heading here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputes as to rights in or to inventions or patents (heading: section 25/26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act addresses disputes concerning rights in or to inventions or patents (heading included among application provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are statutory procedures for determining competing entitlement/disputes — see the relevant sections for procedures and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership of applications (heading: section 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act includes a provision on joint ownership of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint ownership rules govern multiple applicants/co-inventors; consult full section for details on rights and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of application for a patent (heading: section 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a statutory requirement as to the form of application for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be in the prescribed form and include prescribed information; see regulations/section for exact content/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority (heading: section 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act contains provisions governing claiming priority from earlier applications in convention countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and substantive rules on claiming priority (timing, evidence) are set out in the Act and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of specification (heading: section 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act prescribes contents required in provisional and complete specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications must include prescribed disclosures (description, claims, drawings where necessary); see section 32 and regulations for exact content and formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority dates (heading: section 31 and definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act sets rules governing how priority dates are determined and used for novelty/inventive-step assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority date rules determine the relevant 'state of the art' cutoff; amendments modify some definitions — consult full sections for mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examinations of applications and specifications (heading: section 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides for examination of applications and specifications by the patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination procedures (substantive examination, formalities) are legally required; adverse examination results trigger procedural remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if result of examination is adverse (heading: section 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are statutory procedures to follow when examination results are adverse to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes right to be informed, opportunity to amend/respond, and possible appeals or further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to refuse applications in particular cases (heading: section 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar/commissioner has power to refuse applications in particular cases as provided by the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal grounds include non-compliance with statutory patentability/formal requirements; specific cases and processes set out in Act/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure in case of amendment or lodging of fresh application (heading: section 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act prescribes procedure for amendment of applications or lodging of fresh applications related to the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timelines, possible post-dating of specifications, and constraints to prevent extension of subject-matter beyond original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances in which complete specifications may be changed (heading: section 37-38)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act lists circumstances in which complete specifications may be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to specifications are regulated; typically allowed to correct errors or clarify but not to add new matter that extends beyond the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of obtaining and effect of patent of addition (heading: section 39)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides for 'patent of addition' — manner of obtaining and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent of addition relates to improvements; special rules apply for filing, term, and relationship to main patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lapsing of applications and disposal of specifications (heading: section 40-41)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act sets out when applications lapse and how specifications in lapsed applications are to be disposed of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for dealing with lapsed filings, including publication, return of documents, or transfer, are regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication of acceptance and public inspection (heading: section 42-43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act requires notice and publication when a complete specification is accepted and allows inspection by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is published (patent journal) and related documents/specifications become open to inspection per prescribed fees and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications under the PCT (Chapter VA: sections 43A–43F)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act contains provisions on interpretation, effect of international applications designating the Republic, the patent office as receiving/ designated/elected office, national processing, commencement of national phase, and administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT national phase entry, treatment of international applications, and procedural conformity with PCT obligations are governed by these sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting and sealing of patent (heading: section 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides that granted patents are to be sealed and formally issued as certificates in the prescribed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal grant procedures and issuance requirements are regulated; patent certificate is evidence of grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent (heading: section 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act sets out the legal effect and rights conferred by a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee's exclusive rights and scope of protection derive from the patent as granted and documented in the register/specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of patent (heading: section 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act prescribes the duration (term) of patents and related rules (including transitional rules for patents granted under repealed law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term calculation, renewal fees, and limits on extensions are provided in statute and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed patent and rights of restored patentee (sections 47–48)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides for restoration of lapsed patents and sets out the rights of a patentee after restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration procedures, conditions, and the scope of rights after restoration are set out (including possible limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership in patents (heading: section 49)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act contains rules on joint ownership of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint ownership implicates co-proprietor rights, licensing and exercise of rights; specific statutory provisions govern co-owners' relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical errors, amendment of documents, rectification of register (heading: section 50?)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act allows correction of clerical errors and amendment of patent documents and rectification of the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures exist to correct administrative errors in patents or the register to reflect true rights/status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licences of right, cancellation, and compulsory licences (Chapter VIII: sections 50–58)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides for licences of right, cancellation of endorsements, compulsory licences in respect of dependent patents or abuse, termination of contracts relating to licences and effect of licences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory framework governs voluntary and compulsory licensing, grounds for compulsory licences (e.g., dependent patents, abuse of rights), and contractual terminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment, attachment, hypothecation and devolution of patents (Chapter IX: sections 59–60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act regulates assignment, attachment and hypothecation of patents or applications and assignment/devolution by operation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers, security interests, and succession in title to patents are to be recorded in the register per prescribed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for revocation (Chapter X: sections 61–64)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides grounds for application for revocation of patents, treatment of patents comprising more than one invention, and related procedures (including voluntary surrender).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation may be sought for statutory grounds (e.g., lack of novelty/industrial applicability/ inventive step, added matter, fraud) and procedures for hearings/appeals are prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings for infringement and remedies (Chapter XI: sections 65–71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides for proceedings for infringement, restrictions on recovery of damages, presumptions regarding new substances, relief for infringement of partially valid specification, declarations as to non-infringement, acts of non-infringement and special provisions for vessels/aircraft/land vehicles of convention countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil remedies (injunctions, damages) and procedural rules for enforcement/infringement litigation are statutory; special presumptions and limitations apply in certain contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for groundless threats of infringement proceedings (section 70 heading)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides remedies where groundless threats of infringement proceedings have been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets of baseless threats can seek relief (e.g., declaratory relief or damages) under statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and certificates as evidence (Chapter XII: sections 72–74)
rubrics_metrics.description: The register is to be evidence; certificates of the registrar are prima facie evidence; certification of validity provisions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries in the register and registrar-issued certificates carry evidentiary weight in legal proceedings; mechanisms for certification of validity are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to commissioner and the court (Chapter XIII: sections 75–77)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals from registrar to commissioner and from commissioner to the court are provided, and parties may agree to accept commissioner's decision as final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory appellate routes and finality-agreement provisions govern review of administrative patent decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of rights by the State and secrecy requirements (Chapter XIV: sections 78–80)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may acquire inventions or patents and the Minister may require inventions to be kept secret in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory acquisition and national security/secrecy measures apply; terms and compensation/conditions are prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offences and penalties (Chapter XV: sections 81–85 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act prescribes offences and penalties for making false entries in the register, making/producing/tendering false entries or copies, making false statements to deceive or influence the commissioner/registrar/officer, trafficking in patents by officers or employees of the patent office, improper use of the words 'patent office', and other false representations (e.g., falsely representing an article is patented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties include fines and imprisonment (examples: fines up to R1 000 and imprisonment up to 12 months in specified offences; other fines/penalties may apply elsewhere in the Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking / representation offense (section 85)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who (a) falsely represents that any article is a patented article; or (b) represents that any article is the subject of a patent application, knowing that no such application has been made or that an application made has been refused/withdrawn/lapsed, shall be guilty of an offence and liable to fine or imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also covers stamping/marking with 'patent' wording; defenses include good-faith disposition in ordinary course of trade with disclosure of source when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents may be sent by post (section 86)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice or document authorized or required to be lodged, made or given at the patent office, to the registrar or any other person may be delivered by hand or sent through the post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits postal filing/service in addition to in-person delivery; follow prescribed methods where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address for service (section 87)
rubrics_metrics.description: With every application/notice/document, the applicant shall furnish an address within the Republic as an address for service; documents may be served by leaving or sending to that address; the address may be changed by notice in prescribed manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining a valid address for service within the Republic is mandatory for service of process/communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of periods of time (section 88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods specified as running from doing an act commence on the day after the act; if the last day falls on a day the patent office is closed, the act may be done on the next following open day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default timeline computation rules apply; adjust for weekends/office closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condonation or correction of irregularities in procedure (section 89)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar or the commissioner may authorize condonation or correction of any irregularity in procedure in proceedings before him, provided such condonation/correction is not detrimental to any person's interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion to forgive procedural missteps if no prejudice results; application likely required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain contract conditions declared null and void (section 90(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any condition in a contract relating to sale of a patented article or to a licence under a patent that has effects such as (a) prohibiting/restricting purchaser/licensee from purchasing/using articles from others; (b) prohibiting/restricting licensee from using articles/processes not protected by the patent; (c) requiring purchaser/licensee to acquire articles not protected by the patent; (d) requiring purchaser to observe a specified minimum resale price; or (e) prohibiting/restricting making/using the invention in countries where not patented — shall be null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-tying and anti-competition protective provisions: certain post-sale restraint/tying/minimum resale price clauses are unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted exceptions to section 90 (section 90(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in section 90 shall affect conditions prohibiting sale of goods other than those of a particular person, or a lease/licence condition reserving right to supply new replacement parts (other than ordinary articles of commerce) required for repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow exceptions for exclusive supplier contracts and spare-parts reservations in lease/licence contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations-making power (section 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may make regulations prescribing fees/tariffs, procedure in proceedings before registrar/commissioner, service of notices/documents, conduct and administration of the patent office (including recordkeeping/destruction), contents of applications/forms, and generally matters necessary or expedient to give effect to the Act and the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of forms, fees, administrative practice and procedural rules are delegated to regulations; applicants/practitioners must consult current regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register content requirements (section 10(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The register shall record names and addresses of applicants and grantees, inventors of relevant inventions and classification of patents according to subject-matter, and such other particulars as may be prescribed; copies of deeds/agreements/licences affecting patents must be supplied for filing; registrar shall maintain prescribed indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate recording of proprietors, inventors, classifications and legal instruments is mandatory; prescribed form and filing obligations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and copying restrictions (sections 12–13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Register/documents lodged at the patent office shall, on payment of prescribed fees, be open to inspection by the public during prescribed hours, but this right does not include making copies/extracts by mechanical means except where registrar permits due to circumstances beyond control and undue delay would otherwise result; registrar shall furnish copies or particulars on request for prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public inspection allowed, copying restricted; registrar may supply copies or permit mechanical copying in exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Journal content requirements (section 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar shall arrange for periodical publication of a patent journal which shall contain such details of the contents of all complete specifications accepted as may be required to indicate the nature and purpose of the relevant inventions, and any other matter the registrar may consider desirable or required under the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal must sufficiently indicate the nature/purpose of accepted inventions; the registrar has discretion to publish additional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the registrar re evidence and costs (section 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrar may receive evidence and determine whether by affidavit or viva voce, award costs against any party in proceedings before him, and tax costs according to the prescribed tariff; such awards and taxation are subject to review by the commissioner and may be enforced as if awarded by a judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar has quasi-judicial powers to manage proceedings, award and tax costs, with review avenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to hear interested parties before adverse exercise of discretion (section 16(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any discretionary power is conferred on the registrar or commissioner, he shall not exercise that power adversely to an applicant/objector/other person appearing on the register as interested, without, if so required, giving that person an opportunity of being heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic audi alteram partem procedural safeguard for discretionary exercises affecting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extension power (section 16(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any time is specified within which any act or thing is to be done, the registrar or the commissioner may, save where otherwise expressly provided, extend the time either before or after its expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar/commissioner have discretion to extend deadlines unless expressly barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: General powers of the commissioner (section 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner has all such powers and jurisdiction as a single judge in a provincial division of the Supreme Court in civil actions, including appellate power; may order parties to furnish security for costs and may have regard to prospects of success or bona fides; costs awarded by commissioner taxed by registrar subject to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner enjoys broad judicial-style powers to adjudicate patent disputes and manage security/costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and venue for proceedings before commissioner (section 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings before the commissioner shall, save as otherwise provided, be before the commissioner in the first instance; hearings to be held at designated place in Pretoria unless commissioner finds another place more convenient; commissioner may punish willful interruptions/insults/misbehaviour with imprisonment or fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralised adjudication before the commissioner with venue discretion and powers to maintain order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to follow Supreme Court procedure as far as practicable (section 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure in connection with proceedings before the commissioner shall, as far as practicable, be in accordance with law governing procedure in civil cases in the Transvaal Provincial Division of the Supreme Court; where no relevant provision exists, commissioner acts to do substantial justice and carry out objects of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural norms borrow from civil procedure; commissioner has residual discretionary powers to do justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and signature requirement by agent (section 9 & 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to any matter under this Act (other than proceedings in any division of the Supreme Court) may be represented only by an agent; no complete specification shall be accepted and no application to amend a complete specification allowed unless it has been signed by an agent. No person shall practise as a patent agent/attorney unless registered; no one may hold themselves out as such unless registered or in specified partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict rules on professional representation and formal requirement that complete specifications be signed by a registered agent; unauthorised practice is an offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and registration of patent agents and patent attorneys (section 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons may be registered as patent agents on passing the prescribed examination and paying the prescribed fee; persons entitled to practise as attorneys may on passing prescribed examination and fee be registered as patent attorneys; transitional provisions for those registered under repealed law exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrance to the profession requires passing prescribed exams and payment; attorneys have route to registration; transitional grandfathering applied at commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examination Board functions and powers (section 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Board to prescribe syllabuses, minimum qualifications, period of instruction, grant exemptions, recognize examinations, arrange training/instruction/testing, impose disciplinary rules, appoint examiners/moderators, conduct prescribed examination and issue certificates; publish matters in the journal; determine fees/remuneration with concurrence of Minister of Finance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board controls education/assessment/discipline for agents; its prescriptions govern professional qualification/training/examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileges of attorneys (transitional representation) (section 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person entitled to practise as an attorney may, during a period of five years from commencement (or further period up to five years as registrar allows), have rights of representing a party in proceedings under this Act as they had under the repealed law, subject to application/consultation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary transitional rights for attorneys to represent in patent matters, after which registration as agent/attorney required to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal, suspension and discipline of patent agents/attorneys (section 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar or the South African Institute of Intellectual Property Law may apply to court to remove names from register or suspend persons for conduct considered sufficient; restoration and reprimand/fines permitted; notices to institute proceedings must be given to the Institute and law society; publication of orders in the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal disciplinary processes with notice and rights to be heard; court may impose removal/suspension and lesser sanctions; restoration procedures exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may practise and prohibitions (section 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall practise as a patent agent/attorney unless registered; may not hold himself out as such unless registered or if practising as attorney in partnership with a registered patent attorney; restrictions on employing removed/suspended persons; offences and penalties apply for contraventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict licencing regime with criminal penalties for unauthorised practice and restrictions on employing disbarred individuals.
